Mockup for sign-off · 24 Sep 2026

A business unit chooses how it plans

Every picture is taken from the running platform. The proposed ones are the real pages with the change laid over them. Retail Stores and Online Shop are switched only to show the shapes.

What was agreed

  • Each business unit picks how it plans: Pillars, Projects, or Objectives & actions. These are the three ways a supporting function can already plan.
  • The Structure page's Pillars tick for business units becomes the default for new units. A unit's own choice wins.
  • Moving a unit away from pillars hides them and keeps them. Moving back brings them back as they were.
  • A unit not planning in pillars stops counting them. Its score comes from its objectives and from its actions or projects.

1. Setup › Business units

The Pillars count column becomes Plans in, with the number of pillars, projects or actions underneath. The choice itself is made in the row's Edit details dialog, like every other field on this table.

2. Setup › Structure

The per-unit Pillars dot stops being a separate switch. It shows the unit's own choice as a word, so one fact is set in one place. The level's Pillars tick stays as the default for new units.

3. Strategy › Plan, planning in objectives & actions

Online Shop's Plan section shows its dated actions, with owner and due month. Its key objectives stay on the Foundation, exactly where a unit's objectives live today. There is no pillar rail.

4. Strategy › Plan, planning in projects

Retail Stores' Plan section shows the projects rail, with deliverables, outcomes and milestones, and codes in the unit's own letters (RS01). This is the same page a supporting function in projects uses. The content here is borrowed from Finance's plan, only to show the shape.

5. Performance

Today a unit has three headline numbers: objectives, pillars and delivery. A unit in objectives & actions has two cards: objectives, which stays the primary score, and actions done. The pillar number and its breakdown are gone. A unit in projects gets the same two cards, with projects in place of actions.

Needs your answer before building

  1. Switching warns first. When a unit that holds pillars is switched away, a confirmation in the platform's own style says: "Mobile's 4 pillars will be hidden and kept. Switching back brings them back." Agree?
  2. Functions work differently. Switching a supporting function's way of planning archives what was there. For units, you chose hidden and kept. Keep that difference, or make functions hide-and-keep too, so one control behaves one way?
  3. The group's roll-up. A unit with no pillars adds nothing to the group's pillar figures. Its objectives and delivery still count as today. Agree?
  4. Reporting, the deck and the workbooks follow the choice. Each uses the function's existing version for that way of planning. A unit in projects presents like a function in projects. No new design is needed for these.
